📝 Notes
Mar 11, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
AI Studio sketches were reviewed, showing a visual interface for appointment preparation and emotional mapping, with discussion on refining the abstract dual-lane grief visualization and presenting the fragmented concepts to Melissa.Review of AI Studio SketchesAmir Houieh presented AI Studio sketches focusing on a visual, less text-driven interface, including selective information display, an emotional map, and a timeline for progress. The discussion included the grief navigation visualization, which was deemed too abstract, requiring a better design for the dual-lane approach.Focus Area and Experimental ExercisesA focus area was showcased as an entry point for exercises, with experimental concepts like a mirror practice for self-focus and a grid visualizer for tracking completion over time. Noémi Biró strongly approved of the dual-path visualization, balancing information, design, interaction, and the role of AI.Fragmented Sketches and Review PreparationNoémi Biró presented fragmented sketches, including a loss snapshot, an impact map home screen, and an energy-matched suggestion concept based on reported energy level. It was decided that there was enough material to present to Melissa, and they would reclustered Noémi Biró’s sketches around Amir Houieh’s working prototype.
Details
Initial Check-in and Personal Update: Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró began the meeting with a personal check-in, noting that Amir Houieh was working from a cafe and doing better by attempting to move on from anxieties and issues without letting negative thoughts halt progress. They discussed the challenge of managing anxiety, which Amir Houieh likened to a monster that grows the more one reacts to it, and the importance of keeping life going as much as possible (00:00:00). Amir Houieh acknowledged that Noémi Biró and the team have been helpful, stating they will take things easy (00:02:37).
Review of AI Studio Sketches and Visualization Concepts: Amir Houieh presented a few sketches developed in AI Studio, aiming for a more visual and less text-driven interface for one module. The design idea included making the information shown very selective and relevant, such as displaying the appointment preparation tool only if an appointment is scheduled soon or providing a quick summary of the user's emotional state (00:03:44). Other visualizations included an emotional map, analytical parameters to define metrics, and a timeline to give a sense of progress without demolishing the concept of linearity (00:04:47).
Discussion on Grief Navigation Visualization: The speakers discussed a visual concept related to the healthy way to navigate grief, which involves parallel exercises supporting daily life alongside exercises focused on grief, such as journaling and rituals. Noémi Biró explained that this dual-lane approach creates a healthy context, but Amir Houieh felt the current visualization was too abstract and acknowledged the need for a much better design for this concept. Amir Houieh also outlined the "Showed Up" section, which highlights what the user has done and is meant to be encouraging and motivating (00:05:56).
Focus Area and Experimental Exercises in AI Studio: Amir Houieh showcased a focus area that serves as a layer after the module homepage, providing an entry point for starting exercises. Two experimental exercises were presented, including a "mirror practice" where the camera turns on to let the user focus on themself while potentially reading text or hearing spoken words, and a "grid visualizer" to track exercise completion over time. Amir Houieh noted that the mirror practice visualization was abstract and that they did not get into deep design for the grid visualizer (00:06:57).
Alignment of Sketches and Next Steps: Noémi Biró commented that Amir Houieh's prototype takes their own working ideas and presents them in a more coherent and understandable space (00:09:23). They suggested using Amir Houieh's working example to show navigation and then reorganizing Noémi Biró's own experiments around it, taking screenshots of the prototype to create parallels (00:10:37). Amir Houieh agreed that they were purely random sketches and that they were now ready to see if they should show this material to Melissa (00:09:23).
Noémi Biró's Sketches of Exercises and Tools: Noémi Biró presented several sketches, including a "loss snapshot" exercise for quick check-ins about current feelings that connects to the emotion map, making it easier to move from general feelings to granular descriptions. Other visualizations included an "impact map" as a home screen that highlights recent growth and allows users to tap on categories like "relationships" to access clustered exercises, knowledge base articles, and insights from the user's own notes (00:11:58). Noémi Biró also sketched out a "support circle" exercise connected to boundary phrases for communicating about loss, and conversation resource templates for responding to hurtful comments (00:13:24).
Dual-Path Visualization and Activity Timeline: Noémi Biró presented the idea of visualizing the "dual lane" approach to grief—where the user is part of both grief and life—by showing two paths: "Honoring Loss" (e.g., quiet reflections) and "Gentle Living" (e.g., breathing exercises and daily rhythms). The visualization also included an activity timeline tagged with self-care or mood check-ins, which could display reminders, such as taking extra gentleness if an activity like a virtual group is coming up soon (00:15:01). Amir Houieh expressed strong approval for this visualization, stating it showed a very good balance between information, design, interaction, and the role of AI (00:16:17).
Fragmented Sketches and Preparation for Review: Noémi Biró also showed an energy-matched suggestion concept, where the suggested exercises change based on the user's reported energy level, such as getting a 30-minute walk instead of a 10-minute stretch if they feel "okayish" (00:17:20). The speakers agreed that all the sketches were very fragmented but that there was enough material to present to Melissa. The next step involves walking through the material with Melissa to highlight the most valuable concepts, being selective, and then recurerating the successful ideas for the next iteration (00:18:17).
Conclusion and Next Steps: Noémi Biró decided they would take screenshots from Amir Houieh's prototype and reclustered their own sketches around it . They agreed that they should show Amir Houieh's prototype in action to Melissa, zooming into the parallel visualizations afterward . The next meeting is scheduled for about an hour .
Suggested next steps
Noémi Biró will take some screenshots from Amir Houieh's prototype and reclustered her own experiments around it.
Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró will show the prototype in action and then zoom into the parallel visualizations with Melissa.
Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró will walk through all of the ideas with Melissa to see which ones are valuable.
